title: Attach supplied finite free generators of cone cohomology
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring small in $v$, with derived category as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $f:F\to C$ be a map of cochain complexes of $R$-modules in $v$, and $n,b\in\mathbb Z$ with $n\le b+1$. Suppose $F$ is zero below $n$ and above $b$, its terms are finite free, and $H^i(Q(\operatorname{Cone}(f)))=0$ for $i\ge n$. Put $D=\operatorname{Cone}(f)$ and let $Z^{n-1}(D)$ be the kernel of its outgoing differential. Given a finite free module $P$ in $v$ and $q:P\to Z^{n-1}(D)$ such that $P\xrightarrow{q} Z^{n-1}(D)\to H^{n-1}(D)$ is surjective, there exist $G,g:G\to C,j:F\to G$ with $G$ zero below $n-1$ and above $b$, all its terms finite free, $H^i(Q(\operatorname{Cone}(g)))=0$ for $i\ge n-1$, $g\circ j=f$, and $j^i$ invertible for $i\ge n$. All objects remain in $v$. This statement assumes actual generating cycles and does not select them from a finite homology hypothesis.

proof.text: Put D = Cone(f). Project q followed by the cycle inclusion to obtain a:P→F^n and c:P→C^(n-1). The cone differential formulas give a d_F=0 and a f+c d_C=0. Let A be the single complex with P in degree n, and use a to define k:A→F. The degree -1 cochain with component -c has coboundary k f. Set G=Cone(k), g=desc(k,-c,f), and j=inr(k); the cone identities give j g=f. The terms of G are biproducts A^(i+1)⊕F^i. The single-complex vanishing formulas and the hypotheses give both degree bounds. Identify these biproducts with products to transfer finite freeness. For i≥n the A summand is zero, so the cone projection is inverse to j^i.

Construct t:Cone(f)→Cone(g) from the shifted map j and the identity on C using the cone lift formula and j g=f. In degrees i≥n-1, its component is invertible: its inverse acts by the inverse of j^(i+1) on the first summand and the identity on C^i. Two consecutive invertible components imply that cyclesMap(t,i) is invertible and hence homologyMap(t,i) is epi. For i≥n its source homology is zero, by hvan and homologyFunctorFactors, so its target is zero. For i=n-1, the inclusion u:P→G^(n-1) of the new single-complex summand satisfies u d_G=a j and u g=-c. Therefore the image under t of the supplied cycles is the boundary of -u included in Cone(g)^(n-2). Thus q homologyπ homologyMap(t,n-1)=0. Cancel the assumed epimorphism q homologyπ; homologyMap(t,n-1) is both epi and zero, so its target is zero. Transport all resulting homology vanishings along homologyFunctorFactors.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finiteFree_cone_cycle_attachment (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (C F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) (f : F ⟶ C) (b n : ℤ)
    (hn : n ≤ b + 1) (hlow : F.IsStrictlyGE n) (hupp : F.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hfree : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free R (F.X i) ∧ Module.Finite R (F.X i))
    (hvan : ∀ i : ℤ, n ≤ i → IsZero
      ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj (Q.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone f))))
    (P : ModuleCat.{v} R) [Module.Free R P] [Module.Finite R P]
    (q : P ⟶ (CochainComplex.mappingCone f).cycles (n - 1))
    (hq : Epi (q ≫ (CochainComplex.mappingCone f).homologyπ (n - 1))) :
    ∃ (G : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) (g : G ⟶ C) (j : F ⟶ G),
      G.IsStrictlyGE (n - 1) ∧ G.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free R (G.X i) ∧ Module.Finite R (G.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, n - 1 ≤ i → IsZero
        ((homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj
          (Q.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone g)))) ∧
      j ≫ g = f ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, n ≤ i → IsIso (j.f i))
